correctness.rationale: The basepoint-free quartic parametrization P satisfies the original equation; its nonzero generic polar gradient is proportional to the displayed basepoint-free quintics L. The noncollinear degree-five image of L has map degree one by primality, so the tangent factorization also forces P to have degree one. Consequently the original plane quartic is integral and L normalizes its integral degree-five dual, with the stated equation verified by substitution. /workspace/branches/independent_klein.py independently verified the homogeneous polar/substitution identities, the finite collision and ramification certificates, the no-finite-preimage gcd, and the intrinsic singular ideals on three affine charts. In C=1, the equations g=g_a=g_b=0 give the origin and, where b is nonzero, a=2b^3 and b^7=4, hence (a,b)=(2,4); C=0 has only the other two coordinate vertices. At each vertex the equation is a square times a unit plus a nonzero cube, so it is formally an ordinary cusp. Independently, in C=1 set w=a-2b^3 at the fourth point: g=w^2(w+3b^3)-4b^2(b-4)^7. Taking a formal square root of the unit after division by b^2 gives exactly u^2-v^7 up to rescaling. Normalization yields delta=(1,1,1,3); quotient by the equation and partials gives lengths (2,2,2,7), not (2,2,2,6) in characteristic seven. This concerns the reduced dual of the literal plane model, not a scheme-theoretic limit of characteristic-zero duals.
